Examined units for provider-swift/Tests/ClusterPlacementChecks/PlacementSetupCheck.swift: base lines 1263-1422 and head lines 1-333. The only change (base 1260-1262 → head 1260-1264) is in a test check. It adds a `publicModels: []` argument to ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine and keeps the same assertions. With no public declaration, a family that no record passed is still "not yet qualified", and the passing hand-off family still reads "qualified for public traffic".

The new parameter implies the production publicTrafficLine now takes a public-model declaration that may affect the public-traffic qualification line. That production source is not in this batch.

Integration should verify how a non-empty publicModels list interacts with record-based grants. In particular, check whether declaring a model public can yield a "qualified for public traffic" status, or a coordinator-visible grant, without a passing qualification record for the installed artifact. Such a path would bear on qualification and serving-authorization integrity (A-017, A-016, TB-011, T-054, T-052).

This is a test file, so it adds no runtime attack surface. The rest of the visible test code exercises:
- the debug-only override variables (FORCE_MODE, BENCH_CAP, BENCH_CHIP), which tests show a release build refuses;
- the hand-off opt-in gating;
- artifact-SHA binding for public grants.

No security regression is evidenced within these units.
